mcqs.q: The 'basic structure' doctrine was first propounded in:

options.B: Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala (1973)
options.C: Shankari Prasad vs. Union of India (1951)
options.D: Minerva Mills vs. Union of India (1980)

mcqs.q: The basic structure doctrine limits the amending power of Parliament under which Article?
Before Kesavananda Bharati, in which case(s) did the Supreme Court hold that Parliament could amend any part of the Constitution including Fundamental Rights?

options.A: Shankari Prasad vs. Union of India (1951)
options.B: Sajjan Singh vs. State of Rajasthan (1965)

mcqs.q: In Golaknath vs. State of Punjab (1967), the Supreme Court held that Parliament:

options.B: Could not amend Fundamental Rights so as to take away or abridge them

mcqs.q: The 24th Amendment Act, 1971 was passed to nullify the effect of:
The Kesavananda Bharati judgment was delivered by a bench of how many judges?
The Kesavananda case primarily involved challenges to which amendments?
In Kesavananda Bharati, the Supreme Court overruled Golaknath and held that Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights but cannot:

options.B: Destroy or alter the basic structure of the Constitution

mcqs.q: The phrase 'basic structure' is not defined in the Constitution. The Supreme Court has identified it:

options.B: Illustratively from time to time through various judgments
options.D: Only in the Minerva Mills case

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT an element of the basic structure as identified by the Supreme Court?

options.B: Republican and democratic form of government
options.D: All of the above are basic structure elements

mcqs.q: The concept of 'secular character' as part of the basic structure was explicitly affirmed in:

options.B: S.R. Bommai vs. Union of India
options.D: Indira Nehru Gandhi vs. Raj Narain

mcqs.q: The doctrine of basic structure was first applied to strike down a constitutional amendment in:

options.B: Indira Nehru Gandhi vs. Raj Narain (1975)

mcqs.q: In Indira Gandhi vs. Raj Narain (1975), the Supreme Court struck down which part of the 39th Amendment?

options.A: Placing the election of the Prime Minister and Speaker beyond judicial review

mcqs.q: Which basic features did the Supreme Court invoke to strike down the 39th Amendment in the Indira Gandhi case?

options.A: Free and fair elections, Rule of law, Judicial review

mcqs.q: The 42nd Amendment inserted clauses (4) and (5) in Article 368. What did these clauses provide?

options.A: That no constitutional amendment could be questioned in any court on any ground
options.B: That Parliament's amending power is unlimited

mcqs.q: The Supreme Court in Minerva Mills vs. Union of India (1980) struck down which provisions of the 42nd Amendment?

options.B: The extension of Article 31C to all Directive Principles

mcqs.q: In Minerva Mills, the Supreme Court held that the 'harmony and balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles' is:

options.B: A basic feature of the Constitution

mcqs.q: The Supreme Court in Waman Rao vs. Union of India (1981) held that the basic structure doctrine applies:

options.B: Prospectively, from the date of the Kesavananda judgment (24 April 1973)
options.C: Only to amendments after the 42nd Amendment

mcqs.q: The cut-off date for applying the basic structure test to Ninth Schedule laws is:
In I.R. Coelho vs. State of Tamil Nadu (2007), the Supreme Court held that:

options.A: All laws in the Ninth Schedule are immune from judicial review
options.B: Laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 are open to challenge if they violate the basic structure
options.D: Only Fundamental Rights can be tested against basic structure

mcqs.q: The basic structure doctrine was used to strike down the 99th Amendment (NJAC) because it violated:
The Supreme Court's power of judicial review of constitutional amendments is itself a part of:
Which of the following is a basic feature according to judicial pronouncements? 1. Rule of law 2. Judicial review 3. Free and fair elections 4. Federal character
Any amendment that seeks to destroy or substantially impair judicial review can be struck down because:

options.A: Judicial review is a basic feature

mcqs.q: The Supreme Court struck down the NJAC Amendment (99th) in Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association vs. Union of India (2015) on the ground that it violated:
Which of the following amendments was NOT struck down for violating the basic structure?

options.A: 42nd Amendment's clauses giving unlimited amending power
options.B: 39th Amendment's clause placing PM's election beyond judicial review

mcqs.q: The basic structure doctrine applies to:

options.C: Both constitutional amendments and ordinary laws

mcqs.q: In the Kesavananda case, the 'basic structure' was described as:

options.B: The essential framework and foundational values that cannot be destroyed by amendment

mcqs.q: Justice H.R. Khanna's opinion in Kesavananda is famous for the observation that:

options.A: The power to amend does not include the power to destroy
options.B: The Constitution is a sacred document that cannot be changed
options.C: Fundamental Rights are not part of the basic structure
options.D: The Preamble is the entire Constitution

mcqs.q: The list of basic features is:

options.B: Open-ended and has been expanded by the Supreme Court in various cases
options.C: Limited to what was mentioned in Kesavananda

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an example of a basic feature related to federal structure?

options.B: Distribution of legislative powers between Union and States

mcqs.q: The Supreme Court in S.R. Bommai vs. Union of India (1994) held that 'secularism' is a basic feature and any state government acting contrary to it can be dismissed under:

In L. Chandra Kumar vs. Union of India (1997), the Supreme Court held that the power of judicial review of High Courts under Articles 226 and 227 is a basic feature and struck down the provision that:

options.A: Excluded the jurisdiction of High Courts over decisions of tribunals
options.C: Made tribunals subordinate to the Supreme Court
options.D: Gave tribunals power to review Supreme Court decisions

mcqs.q: The Supreme Court in M. Nagaraj vs. Union of India (2006) upheld reservation in promotions for SCs/STs but required the state to demonstrate:

options.A: Backwardness, inadequacy of representation, and maintenance of efficiency

mcqs.q: The basic structure doctrine does NOT apply to:

options.A: Laws placed in the Ninth Schedule before 24 April 1973
options.C: All laws in the Ninth Schedule

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a basic feature?
The basic structure doctrine has been criticized because:

options.A: It gives the judiciary enormous power to veto amendments without a clear textual basis
options.B: It is defined exhaustively in the Constitution

mcqs.q: The basic structure doctrine is considered essential because it:

options.A: Prevents the abuse of the amending power to destroy the Constitution

mcqs.q: In I.R. Coelho, the Supreme Court held that any law included in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 can be challenged if it violates:

options.B: Any basic feature, not limited to Fundamental Rights

mcqs.q: The basic structure doctrine is often described as the 'safety valve' against:
The Supreme Court in S.R. Bommai used the basic structure doctrine to limit misuse of Article 356, emphasizing that the power under Article 356 is:

options.A: Conditional and subject to judicial review

mcqs.q: The basic structure doctrine is a part of the 'basic structure' itself. This means:

options.A: The doctrine cannot be abolished by a constitutional amendment
options.B: It can be abolished by a simple majority
options.C: It was added by the 42nd Amendment
options.D: It is not recognized by the Supreme Court

mcqs.q: The 42nd Amendment's extension of Article 31C to all Directive Principles was struck down because it destroyed:

options.A: The harmonious balance between Part III and Part IV, a basic feature

mcqs.q: The basic structure doctrine was first conceptualized in the arguments before the Supreme Court in:
Which amendment sought to make Directive Principles superior to Fundamental Rights by amending Article 31C to cover all Directive Principles?
The basic structure doctrine has been applied to:

options.A: Both Union and State constitutional amendments

mcqs.q: The Supreme Court in the Puttaswamy (Right to Privacy) case held that the right to privacy is a Fundamental Right and forms part of the basic structure as it is intrinsic to:

options.A: Dignity of the individual and liberty

mcqs.q: The basic structure doctrine ensures that the Constitution is:

options.A: Supreme and not at the mercy of the legislature

mcqs.q: The Supreme Court's decision in Kesavananda Bharati was a 7:6 verdict. Who among the following delivered the famous dissenting opinion that the amending power is unlimited?
The basic structure doctrine is an example of:

options.A: Judicial innovation to preserve the Constitution's core values
